messages:
anya_ml: ran a long-tail sensitivity scan for INT8 weight-only (bitsandbytes + llm.int8) on Eos-12B today. focused on three slices: short QA, multi-turn math, and small-code generation.

james_engml: nice — environment? bnb version / cuda / torch?

anya_ml: bitsandbytes 0.40, llm.int8 branch v1.3, torch 2.2, CUDA 12.1, single A100-80GB. batch=1 for latency, batch=8 for throughput runs.

priyanka_research: what metrics did you track?

anya_ml: exact-match (EM) for math, F1 for QA, pass@1 for code, plus P95 latency and tokens/sec. also recorded confidence shifts (logit differences) on key tokens.

evalbot: automated run complete. artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/eos12b/int8-longtail/2083456789/; summary CSV + per-slice diffs uploaded.

james_engml: top-line numbers?

anya_ml: short summary:
- QA slice: F1 delta -1.4% vs fp16 (acceptable)
- Math slice: EM delta -6.2% (regression cluster on nested arithmetic prompts)
- Code slice: pass@1 delta -2.1% (mostly formatting tokens)
- P95 latency: +18ms (good), throughput batch8: +2.1x tokens/sec (win)

priyanka_research: math drop is concerning. any pattern in failures?

anya_ml: yes — failures concentrated on long chains of small integer ops and nested parentheses. model emits correct tokens early but drifts after carry-over ops. logit deltas show softer peaks on numeric tokens.

leo_infra: could this be quantization amplification for outlier weights in feed-forward layers?

anya_ml: probably. ran per-layer outlier detector: top 2 FFN layers show >3.5x dynamic range compared to fp16 baseline.

james_engml: did you try mixed strategy (int8 weight-only but keep outlier layers in fp16)?

anya_ml: yes — quick experiment: pin two outlier FFN layers to fp16, rest int8. math EM drop reduced to -1.8%. latency penalty ~+5ms, throughput still +1.9x.

priyanka_research: nice tradeoff. does llm.int8 support that toggling at runtime?

anya_ml: llm.int8 currently supports per-layer dtype overrides via config. I used "layer_dtype_overrides": {"ffn.22":"fp16","ffn.25":"fp16"} in the run config.

ops-bot: deploy note: created rollout candidate eos12b-int8-longtail-v1 with fallback rule for math-slice traffic -> eos12b-fp16.

leo_infra: suggestions for production profile?

anya_ml: recommended profile: default int8 weight-only with per-layer overrides for detected outliers; enable prefix KV caching; add slice-based routing to send flagged math endpoints to fp16 or the mixed profile. Also add a quality regression eval triggered on canary.

james_engml: any quick eval scripts we can add to CI?

anya_ml: pushed a small harness to the run artifacts: run_eval.sh (uses SQuAD-like and math microbench). snippet: 
```bash
python eval/runner.py --model eos12b-int8 --slices short_qa math_chain code_small --out /tmp/eos_int8.csv
```

priyanka_research: also curious if AWQ/GPTQ changes behavior here — can we schedule a small AWQ compare?

anya_ml: noted. I queued an AWQ + GPTQ batch for the same slices; should finish overnight. evalbot will post results.

leo_infra: thanks — leaving a reaction :eyes: on the artifacts. next step: create a canary with per-layer overrides and 5% traffic routing for math-heavy routes.

james_engml: +1. if AWQ resolves the math EM gap we can revisit baseline.

anya_ml: will follow up with AWQ/GPTQ results and a short runbook for ops (how to flip per-layer overrides and routing).
